nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign an integer score to each pair of letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score. For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, the score (with respect to $\sigma$ and $g$) of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ equals the sum, over all columns $c$ of $A$, of the column score of the pair $(c_i, c_j)$.
nodes.title: Score of an induced pairwise alignment

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign an integer score to each pair of letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score. For a column $c$ of a multiple alignment of $k$ sequences, which gives each row $r < k$ either a letter or a gap $c_r$, the sum-of-pairs score of $c$ is $\sum_{i < j < k} s(c_i, c_j)$, where $s$ is the pairwise column score: $\sigma(a, b)$ for letters $a$ and $b$, $g$ for a letter against a gap, and $0$ for two gaps.
nodes.title: Sum-of-pairs score of a column

nodes.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every family of $k$ sequences $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$ whose lengths sum to at most $n$, there is a valid multiple alignment of $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$.
nodes.title: Every family of sequences has a multiple alignment

nodes.summary: For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, deleting the gaps from the first row of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ gives the same sequence as deleting the gaps from row $i$ of $A$.
nodes.title: Letters of the first row of an induced alignment

nodes.summary: For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, deleting the gaps from the second row of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ gives the same sequence as deleting the gaps from row $j$ of $A$.
nodes.title: Letters of the second row of an induced alignment

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a valid multiple alignment of sequences $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$. Then for all rows $i, j < k$, the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ is a valid pairwise alignment of $s_i$ and $s_j$.
nodes.title: Induced pairwise alignments are valid

nodes.summary: For a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, no column of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ is a gap in both rows.
nodes.title: Induced alignments have no all-gap column

nodes.summary: Given a multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences and rows $i, j < k$, the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$ is obtained by keeping, for each column $c$ of $A$ in order, the pair $(c_i, c_j)$, and dropping the columns in which both $c_i$ and $c_j$ are gaps.
nodes.title: Induced pairwise alignment

nodes.summary: A multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ rows is a valid multiple alignment of sequences $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$ when no column of $A$ consists only of gaps and, for every $i < k$, deleting the gaps from row $i$ of $A$ gives $s_i$.
nodes.title: Valid multiple alignment

nodes.summary: Let $\sigma$ assign an integer score to each pair of letters and let $g$ be an integer gap score. For every multiple alignment $A$ of $k$ sequences, the sum-of-pairs score of $A$ equals the sum, over all pairs of rows $i < j < k$, of the score of the pairwise alignment induced by $A$ on rows $i$ and $j$.
nodes.title: The SP score is the sum of the induced pairwise scores

nodes.summary: Fix a score $\sigma(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z}$ for each pair of letters $a, b$ of an alphabet $\alpha$ and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$. Let $s_0, \dots, s_{k-1}$ be sequences over $\alpha$ and let $A$ be a valid multiple alignment of them: no column of $A$ consists only of gaps, and deleting the gaps from row $i$ of $A$ leaves $s_i$. nodes.summary: Fix a score $\sigma(a, b) \in \mathbb{Z}$ for each pair of letters $a, b$ and a gap score $g \in \mathbb{Z}$. For two entries $x, y$, each a letter or a gap, let $s(x, y) = \sigma(x, y)$ if both are letters, $s(x, y) = g$ if exactly one is a gap, and $s(x, y) = 0$ if both are gaps. nodes.title: Sum-of-pairs score

nodes.summary: A multiple alignment with $k$ rows over an alphabet $\alpha$ is a finite list of columns, each of which assigns to every row $i \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$ either a letter of $\alpha$ or a gap. No condition ties the rows to given sequences.
nodes.title: Multiple alignments

nodes.summary: For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, the finite set of all pairs $(i, j)$ with $i, j \in \{0, \dots, k-1\}$ and $i < j$, so that each unordered pair of distinct rows appears exactly once.
nodes.title: Pairs of rows

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
